long_biography.plain_text:
Arab Radio and Television gave Saudi entrepreneur Saleh Abdullah Kamel a hands-on role in regional broadcasting. The pay-TV network carried sport, films and educational programming. A wall of screens in his Jeddah office allowed him to monitor its channels directly, an unusually close arrangement for the founder of a large conglomerate.

Kamel's institution-building extended to economic research and education. He established centres devoted to Islamic economics and served on cultural, charitable and education boards. After his death on 18 May 2020, Al Baraka's board appointed Abdullah Saleh Kamel as chairman the following month, while the banking group's executive management remained separate.

uncertainties: Mortality is verified at 100: Al Baraka's official announcement and Saudipedia give 18 May 2020, while Forbes and major regional reporting independently confirm his death in May 2020. The existing mortality status and death fields are therefore retained without correction.

Sources describe Kamel as 79 or 80 at death because only the 1941 birth year is firmly established and no reliable birth day or month was found. Calculated death-age fields and missing birth day and month remain unproposed.

Saudipedia and The National place his birth in Makkah, while a weaker German-language reference gives Jeddah. The two stronger, independent sources support the Makkah al-Mukarramah proposal at very high confidence.

Aviation & Aerospace is used for wealth creation because historical Forbes reporting says aviation-services contracts produced the bulk of Kamel's fortune. Diversified describes his principal holdings at death because Dallah had developed material businesses across several unrelated sectors.

Forbes classifies the fortune as self-made, but reliable sources do not establish Kamel's family financial platform or starting advantages with enough precision to choose the independent-start or advantaged-start subtype.

Kamel's founder ownership and chairmanship ended with his death. Abdullah Saleh Kamel already held a Dallah executive role and was appointed Al Baraka Banking Group chairman in June 2020; those successor responsibilities and all later family-company activity are not attributed to Saleh Kamel.
The pay-TV network's later transactions and the current ownership of its remaining businesses are not needed to establish Kamel's lifetime founder role and are excluded from the biographies.
No identity-verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website was found. Organisational and memorial accounts were not substituted for personal profiles.

Politics, allegations, legal matters, controversy, private-family trivia, religious commentary beyond the directly material banking and economics context, rankings, net-worth figures and vessel material are excluded from the biographies.
